blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Adaptive robot perception systems must balance detector accuracy, inference latency, and energy consumption, particularly when high ambient temperatures cause processors to thermally throttle. We propose Thermal-Headroom Routing (THR), a lightweight model-selection policy that forecasts processor temperature using a closed-form RC thermal model and excludes detector configurations predicted to cross a throttling threshold. We evaluate THR with four YOLO11 configurations across seven real-world perception traces, eight ambient temperatures, and 20 randomized seeds, comparing it with latency-aware routing, fixed-threshold thermostats, duty caps, and a matched-compute-budget control. At ambient temperatures of 45-55 degrees C and a tight inference deadline, THR eliminates throttling in simulation, reduces deadline misses by 3.9-7.5 percentage points, and reduces energy per on-time frame by approximately 12-13% relative to a latency-belief router. A separate experiment using deadline-paced, nonoverlapping frame execution yields miss-rate reductions of 6.2-9.5 percentage points. A tuned thermostat or duty cap can match THR at a fixed operating point; predictive routing is most useful when ambient conditions or calibrated thermal parameters differ from those used to tune static policies. Measurements on an Apple M5 support the single-node heating approximation but do not validate hardware throttling. The results characterize the conditions under which thermal forecasting improves the efficiency and timeliness of resource-constrained robot perception.
blocks.zh: 适应性机器人感知系统必须平衡探测器的准确性,推论延迟性和能耗,特别是当高环境温度导致处理器受热节流时. 我们建议采用热-头室跑道(THR),这是一种轻量级模型选择政策,利用封闭式RC热能模型预测处理器温度,并排除预计会突破节能阈值的探测器配置。 我们用四个YOLO11的配置来评估THR, 覆盖7个真实世界的感知痕迹,8个环境温度,20个随机化的种子, 将其与耐久感知的路由,固定阈值的恒温器,值班上限, 以及匹配的计算预算控制进行比较。 在环境温度为45-55摄氏度且推论期限很紧的情况下,THR在模拟中消除了节奏,将最后期限误差降低3.9-7.5个百分点,相对于一个纬度-信仰路由器,每个时段的能耗减少约12-13%. 使用最后期限节奏、非重叠框架执行的单独试验得出6.2-9.5个百分点的误差率。 调温器或值电上限可以在固定操作点与THR相匹配;当环境条件或调温参数不同于调静政策时,预测路径最有用。 苹果M5上的测量支持单节点加热近似,但不验证硬件节流. 研究结果说明了热能预报在何种条件下能提高资源受限机器人感知的效率和及时性。

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en:
Consider a Jetson-class module in a sealed enclosure on a robot in the
Sonoran Desert, with the air at 45 °C. If the perception stack runs
its largest detector on every frame, the chip reaches its throttle
limit in about a minute. The governor then down-clocks it, and the
small models slow down along with the large one until the chip cools [ 1 , 2 ] . In our simulations a
policy that always runs the large model goes 12.5 s without an on-time
detection at 45 °C and 91 s at 55 °C. Fig. 1 shows one
two-minute mission at 45 °C: a router that reacts to latency drives
the chip into repeated throttle cycles, and THR keeps it just under the
line.

blocks.en:
Adaptive inference is the usual answer to a tight latency budget.
Early-exit networks and routers choose cheaper computation per input or
per frame [ 3 , 4 , 5 ] ,
and contention-aware detectors such as ApproxDet [ 6 ] also watch the load from co-located applications. These systems react
to latency once it has risen. On a hot chip that signal arrives late,
because the slowdown was caused by earlier choices and lasts tens of
seconds. Thermal-aware DVFS [ 7 ] and thermal-aware
multi-DNN scheduling on phones [ 8 ] address heat by
controlling frequency or placement. We ask a narrower question that
matters for robots with a fixed set of detector configurations: how
should the router itself use temperature, and how much does a
temperature forecast add over simpler rules? Belief-space perception
routing [ 9 ] , which this work extends, left
thermal effects out of its contention model.

blocks.en:
Our contributions:
(i) a closed-loop model of thermal contention for adaptive inference,
in which the router’s configuration choice sets the power input to an
RC thermal node with a hysteretic throttle (§ III );
(ii) THR, a closed-form rule that keeps the forecast temperature under
the throttle limit at about 7 μ \mu s per frame (§ IV );
(iii) an evaluation against baselines chosen to beat it: a thermostat,
duty caps tuned offline, a matched-budget control in the spirit of the
matched-input controls of [ 10 ] , a deadline
sweep, and five variations of the true chip, with 20 seeds and Holm
correction (§ VI ); and
(iv) an account of where THR helps and where it does not. Its gain
over latency-only routing comes from rationing the heavy model. The
forecast itself pays off when the chip heats differently from what a
fixed rule assumed, and with deadline slack, throttling costs less than
rationing does.

blocks.en:
Adaptive and efficient inference. Early-exit networks [ 3 , 4 ] , dynamic
transformers [ 5 ] and early exiting for driving [ 11 , 12 , 13 ] vary computation with
the input. Modality gating [ 14 , 15 , 16 ] decides which sensors to process. ApproxDet [ 6 ] selects detection branches under a latency SLA using measured
contention from co-located apps. In all of these the compute budget is
fixed or observed. None treats it as a state the policy’s own choices
drive.

Thermal behaviour of edge inference. On a Raspberry Pi, long
CNN runs throttle within seconds without active cooling, and outdoor
ambients between 22 and 36 °C change throughput by up to 27.7% [ 2 ] . A Jetson AGX Orin in an outdoor
enclosure throttled under a synthetic stress test at a +40 °C
setpoint (GPU 95.6 °C, CPU 99.0 °C), while a YOLOv8 workload drew
about half the power and stayed below the threshold [ 17 ] . Throttling therefore depends on the model,
the cooling and the duty cycle, which is why we sweep the plant
parameters below. Measurements on phone SoCs show throttling dominating
sustained performance [ 1 ] .

Thermal management. HotSpot-style RC models [ 18 ] and temperature-aware MPSoC scheduling [ 19 ] predict hot spots and schedule around
them. zTT [ 7 ] learns CPU/GPU frequency settings with
reinforcement learning so that phones avoid throttling. Phoenix [ 8 ] combines processor placement with multi-exit
networks to delay throttling for multi-DNN video apps. THR works one
level up: it leaves the governor alone and chooses among detector
configurations using a temperature forecast. It could run on top of a
DVFS policy like zTT.

blocks.en: VI-E Physically consistent frame timing

blocks.en:
In E11 each decision lasts one deadline period D D of wall-clock time.
The thermal plant integrates over Δ ​ t = D \Delta t=D per decision. At each
decision the router takes the newest recorded frame, so decision k k uses the trace frame at time k ​ D kD and the frames in between are
skipped, as in a latest-frame robot pipeline. Inference still running
at the next boundary is abandoned, so work never overlaps, and THR’s
horizon stays 5 s of wall-clock time (15 to 24 decisions). Missions
are 1200 decisions, 4.2 to 6.8 minutes. Policies, seeds and the
88 °C thermostat are unchanged, and the 45 °C cap is retuned
under the new timing.

blocks.en: VII Discussion and Limitations
blocks.zh: 七. 讨论和限制

blocks.en:
Reading the temperature is what keeps a router out of throttling;
routers that only watch latency throttle in every hot run we tried. At
one ambient on a known chip, the share of heavy-model frames sets the
accuracy-timeliness point, and a thermostat or duty cap at the right
setting does as well as THR. The forecast earns its place when the
ambient changes or the chip heats faster or settles hotter than the rule
assumed. In those runs the thermostat and the fixed caps throttled and
THR did not, which is the claim we make for it. On a chip that has
been characterized well, a tuned rule is just as good.

The deadline matters as much as the temperature. With the deadline at
the large model’s median latency, avoiding throttling reduces misses
and energy. With 25% slack, the cheaper models absorb throttling, and
a latency-only router delivers more on-time accuracy than THR.
Deployments should check which side of that line they are on.

blocks.en: VIII Conclusion
blocks.zh: 八 结论

blocks.en:
On a hot robot, choosing the large detector now can cause throttling a
minute later. THR gives the router a closed-form temperature forecast
that costs microseconds per frame. With a tight deadline it kept the
chip out of throttling on all seven traces at 45 and 55 °C and cut
deadline misses by 3.9 to 7.5 percentage points and energy per on-time
frame by 12 to 13% relative to latency-only routing. A tuned thermostat
reaches the same operating points on the chip it was tuned for, but
throttled for up to 29% of the mission on a chip 20% hotter than
assumed, where THR stayed at zero. With deadline slack, throttling is
cheap and THR’s rationing is not worth its accuracy cost. For teams
building perception on hot hardware, the practical advice is to give
the router a temperature input, and to use a forecast when the chip’s
thermal behaviour is uncertain.
